chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleym al-Farra', from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly.

Except that he said in his hadith: When the angel said, 'Its Lord made me enter it,' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recognized that he was the Angel of Death (peace be upon him). So he said to him, 'What brought you down?' He said, 'I have come to give good news to a man that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has taken as a close friend.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So who is this man?' The angel said to him, 'And what do you want from him?' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will serve him for the days of my life.' The angel said to him, 'You are he.'

key_terms.أَهْبَطَكَ: What brought you down / descended you

ai.seo_question: Who is the man that Allah took as a close friend in the story of Prophet Ibrahim?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, the Angel of Death reveals to Prophet Ibrahim that he himself is the 'Khalil' (Close Friend) of Allah, a title that underscores Ibrahim's supreme spiritual station in Shia tradition. Ibrahim’s immediate offer to serve him illustrates the profound humility and self-effacement characteristic of the prophets, while the angel's recognition of Ibrahim's identity highlights the divine intimacy granted to the Khalil. This incident serves as a theological affirmation of Ibrahim's unique closeness to God, distinguishing him as the ultimate exemplar of servitude and friendship with the Divine.
